OpenJade and other SGML tools build on it. The pyexpat oracle is a different family, so the match is cross-family.

name: rapidxml
license_evidence: https://deb.debian.org/debian/pool/main/r/rapidxml/rapidxml_1.13.orig.tar.gz (rapidxml-1.13/license.txt: Boost Software License 1.0 or MIT, chosen by the user)
input_api: rapidxml::xml_document<>::parse<0>(char*) on a mutable, zero-terminated local byte buffer; RapidXML parses in situ (it modifies the buffer) and does no namespace processing, so the adapter copies the input, appends the terminator and resolves prefixes from in-scope xmlns attributes
source_note: Debian's unmodified upstream 1.13 tarball (SHA-256 36237604b5cd34424d8537ba9411f9f2cca842cdcb88c956c5bf39ce243bb44b); rapidxml.hpp, rapidxml_utils.hpp and license.txt are byte-identical to SourceForge rapidxml-1.13.zip.
scope: XML UTF-8 from a local mutable, zero-terminated buffer up to 1 MiB parsed in situ into RapidXML's DOM with parse flags 0 (entity and character references translated; processing instructions and DOCTYPE not kept as nodes; no validation or DTD expansion); Namespaces in XML resolved by the adapter, not RapidXML; attributes sorted per element to match the control oracle
family_note: Header-only rapidxml.hpp supplies the parser and DOM with no Xerces-C++, pugixml, TinyXML2, libxml2 or expat dependency; a distinct parser engine. Boost.PropertyTree's XML reader embeds a RapidXML-derived copy (boost/property_tree/detail/xml_parser_read_rapidxml.hpp) and is not an independent engine. RapidXML preserves qualified names; namespace resolution is adapter code, as in the pugixml and TinyXML2 adapters.

not_verified: Two small valid namespace-aware UTF-8 controls do not establish complete XML 1.0, DTD/entity, other encoding, processing-instruction node or malformed-input behavior. The order control's processing instruction is skipped by the default parse flags, not exposed as a node.
verification_note: RapidXML parses in situ: xml_document<>::parse<0>(char*) writes into the caller's mutable, zero-terminated buffer, so the adapter parses a copy. RapidXML keeps qualified names; namespace resolution is adapter code. Both shared valid controls pass; the default flags skip the order control's processing instruction instead of exposing it as a node. The control run covers 413 rapidxml.hpp lines; the parser-only AFL++ probe gives 38 and 45 repeat-stable tuples on the two controls (difference 15). Adoption is weak: Debian librapidxml-dev has 17 installations, none with recent use, and vendored or Boost.PropertyTree-embedded copies are not counted. Boost.PropertyTree's reader is RapidXML-derived, not a separate engine.
